name: Titan II GLV
dispatch: The Titan II that launched Gemini was, like Mercury's rockets, a converted weapon — America's largest intercontinental missile, man-rated to carry a crew. Its defining trait was its fuel: where cryogenic propellants have to be loaded just before launch and can force a scrub, the Titan burned storable liquids that let it sit ready and lift off close to on time. That reliability of timing mattered more than it sounds, because Gemini's whole job was rendezvous, and catching another spacecraft in orbit depends on launching at an exact moment. The workhorse of the program, it flew all ten crewed Geminis without losing a crew.
description: Titan II GLV is a orbital launcher built by Martin Marietta in USA. Workhorse for Project Gemini. Retired after first flight in 1964.
